title: Continuous Audit and Assurance
answer: Ledger anomaly detection, substantive testing, inventory observation, going concern analysis and controls testing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Ledger Anomaly Detection
children.blurb: Ledger anomaly detection is the practice of scanning journal entries, subledgers and transaction streams for items that do not fit the expected pattern of a business.

children.name: Substantive Testing at Full Coverage
children.blurb: Substantive testing at full coverage means testing every transaction or balance in a population rather than sampling a subset of it.

children.name: Inventory Observation and Valuation
children.blurb: Inventory observation and valuation covers the work of confirming that reported stock exists, is owned or controlled, and is carried at an amount the accounts can support.

children.name: Going Concern Analysis
children.blurb: Going concern analysis is the work of judging whether a company can meet its obligations for at least the next twelve months, and it sits inside continuous audit and assurance because the judgement now has to be refreshed between reporting dates rather than once a year.

children.name: Internal Control Testing
children.blurb: Internal control testing is the work of checking whether the controls a company says it relies on actually operate as described.

sections.body: Continuous audit and assurance applies machine learning to the evidence an audit runs on: the general ledger, the transaction stream, the inventory count, the control log. In practice this means models that score journal entries for unusual combinations of user, time, amount and account, and that flag patterns a sampling approach would miss. It also means testing whole populations rather than a sample, so every invoice, payment and adjustment is examined and the exceptions are ranked for a human to review. Inventory work uses image and sensor data to compare what is on a shelf or in a yard against what the system says is there. Going concern work looks for deterioration signals in cash flow, covenant headroom and customer payment behaviour. The aim is not to remove the auditor but to move the auditor's attention to the cases that matter.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Anomaly detection on ledgers is the most mature part, and it works best where the data is clean and the baseline behaviour is stable. Full population testing is now practical for large transaction sets, though the hard part is not running the test but deciding which exceptions are real and documenting why the rest were cleared. Inventory observation through computer vision is promising but sensitive to lighting, occlusion and the difference between what a camera sees and what a valuation policy means. Going concern analysis remains a judgement problem, and models can surface warning signs without settling whether a business can continue. Control testing is partly automatable, especially where logs are structured, but many controls live in human behaviour and email. The honest limits are data quality, explainability, and the fact that an auditor still signs the opinion.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the audit from raw records to the final judgement. Ledger Anomaly Detection is the entry point, covering how unusual entries are found in the transaction stream. Substantive Testing at Full Coverage takes that further, showing how whole populations replace samples and what that changes about evidence. Inventory Observation and Valuation deals with physical assets, where counting and pricing meet. Going Concern Analysis sits at the level of the entity, asking what the numbers say about survival. Internal Control Testing closes the loop by examining whether the controls that produce the data can be trusted. A reader new to the area should start with ledger anomaly detection, then move to substantive testing, and treat the other three as the places where the method meets the physical world, the future of the business, and the systems that generate the evidence.
